pathway.title: AMERICAN AIRLINES, INC. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage is high because earnings fell, not because debt grew. Reported EBITDA fell from USD 4,573 million in FY2024 to USD 2,916 million over the last twelve months while debt stayed near USD 25,876 million, taking total debt to 8.87x; unhedged fuel and contract-bound labour costs pass price shocks straight into EBITDA, so creditors carry fuel risk without a cushion. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04

- Interest cover is thin. Interest paid took 48.56% of last-twelve-month EBITDA, so cover of 2.06x leaves little room before cash interest competes with maturities and aircraft deliveries for liquidity. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02

- Liquidity is the main protection but is finite. USD 11,763 million of available liquidity covers the USD 4,181 million of principal due before the end of 2027 by 2.81x, yet it only matches the USD 12,042 million due through 2028, so access to refinancing, not cash on hand, decides the 2028 outcome. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C03

- Recent cash flow is flattered by customer-funded balances. Free cash flow of USD 1,780 million in the first nine months of 2026 came with a USD 3,206 million rise in air traffic and loyalty liabilities, which unwind if bookings slow. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06

- Support from the parent is real but runs both ways. The parent guarantees the issuer's credit facilities and the AAdvantage financing and no dividend is evidenced, yet the issuer has lent USD 12,512 million net to the parent, so the issuer's liquidity is partly a claim on the parent group. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07

runs.text: Ranked weaknesses. First, high leverage driven by fuel: reported EBITDA of USD 2,916 million over the last twelve months against debt of USD 25,876 million gives 8.87x, and unhedged fuel passes price shocks directly to earnings, which leaves little capacity to absorb another shock. Second, thin cover of 2.06x with interest paid at 48.56% of EBITDA, which raises the cost of any shortfall. Third, a 2028 maturity of USD 7,861 million that exceeds what liquidity covers alone. Fourth, debt that is entirely secured, with 55.75% linked to aircraft and engines, so more borrowing adds claims on the same collateral. Fifth, a net receivable from the parent of USD 12,512 million, which makes the issuer's cash partly dependent on the parent's credit. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C07; calculation C09

Ranked strengths. First, liquidity of USD 11,763 million including USD 7,159 million of short-term investments, which covers principal due before the end of 2027 by 2.81x. Second, a network and loyalty business in which loyalty revenue was 13.42% of revenue and partners paid USD 6.2 billion of cash to the group in 2025, a recurring source that supports financing against loyalty assets. Third, demonstrated refinancing access in 2026, when revolvers were extended to 2031, a term loan to 2033 and three aircraft certificate programs were placed. Fourth, a parent that guarantees key debt and paid no dividend. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C03; calculation C08

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No acquisition, sponsor transaction or change of control is stated for the issuer, so the summary is of its 2026 debt activity. In February 2026 the 2025 AAdvantage term loan was amended to lower its margin, and in March 2026 the three revolving facilities were re-established with commitments to March 2031. In May 2026 the 2014 term loan was refinanced and increased to a May 2033 maturity, and aircraft and engine financing continued through three pass-through certificate programs in May, June and August 2026 and USD 705 million of new equipment loans. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 257; 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–36

The issuer also retired debt: the short-term term loan, which was due in January 2026, was repaid in full, the 8.50% senior secured notes were prepaid in full, and USD 310 million of equipment notes under earlier pass-through certificates was prepaid. Of the August 2026 certificates, about USD 633 million of proceeds was still held in escrow at September 30, 2026 and is not reported as debt until further equipment notes are issued, so reported debt excludes that amount for now. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; calculation C06

fields.value: Financial foundation for AMERICAN AIRLINES, INC. (american-airlines-inc), as of 2026-11-05, under the credit_snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's own statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics for FY2024, FY2025 and the nine months to September 30, 2026, with the parent's figures kept apart.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt reached 8.87x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA at September 30, 2026, up from 5.63x at the end of 2024, so creditors of American Airlines, Inc. depend on USD 11,763 million of available liquidity and collateral rather than earnings cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has risen because earnings fell, not because borrowing grew. Reported EBITDA moved from USD 4,573 million in FY2024 to USD 3,395 million in FY2025 and USD 2,916 million over the last twelve months, while total debt moved from USD 25,736 million to USD 25,876 million. Fuel explains most of the recent step: aircraft fuel and related taxes rose by USD 4,427 million, or 55.22%, in the first nine months of 2026, and operating income was USD 535 million against USD 1,042 million a year earlier. The nine-month EBITDA margin fell to 4.21% from 6.05%, so the fuel price path is the main swing factor for leverage: lower prices would help and higher prices would extend the deterioration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover has slipped more gently than leverage, from 2.53x in FY2024 to 2.19x in FY2025 and 2.06x over the last twelve months, because interest paid fell from USD 1,806 million in FY2024 to USD 1,551 million in FY2025 and USD 1,416 million over the last twelve months as the issuer repaid higher-cost debt. That offset is finite: cover on reported EBITDA is thin for a business whose fixed charges also include aircraft rent and large purchase commitments, and interest paid is not a fixed-charge measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the main support for creditors. At September 30, 2026 American reported USD 11,763 million of available liquidity, being cash of USD 1,094 million, short-term investments of USD 7,159 million and undrawn facilities of USD 3,510 million, against USD 4,181 million of principal due before the end of 2027, a cover of 2.81x. The wall is heavier in 2028 at USD 7,861 million, so the test is whether liquidity is preserved or refinancing is available when that year approaches. The filing summarises minimum-liquidity and collateral-value covenants but prints no headroom, and undrawn facilities are committed lines rather than cash, so covenant capacity is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is flattered by customer-funded balances. Operating cash flow was USD 4,440 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 2,229 million a year earlier, and free cash flow after capital expenditures was USD 1,780 million against USD 126 million. Yet customer-funded balances, being the air traffic liability and both loyalty program liabilities, rose by USD 3,206 million to USD 20,928 million since December 31, 2025. These are obligations to provide travel or miles, they follow the season and they are not interest-bearing debt, so the improvement can reverse if bookings slow or redemptions rise; FY2025 free cash flow was USD -1,786 million after capital expenditures of USD 3,716 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer also lends to its affiliates. Receivables from related parties were USD 10,430 million at September 30, 2026, USD 534 million higher than at year-end, and the 2025 cash flow shows a USD 1,701 million outflow for this line inside operating activities. Repayment terms are not established from the statements, so these balances support group liquidity but their availability to the issuer's own creditors is not shown. Parent debt of USD 29,635 million exceeds the issuer's USD 25,876 million by USD 3,759 million, so the parent's net debt target, which also counts leases and pensions, is on a wider definition than any ratio here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fuel financing of USD 933 million is, as the annual report describes it, a bank facility at one-month SOFR plus 3.75%, secured on a second-priority basis by brand intellectual property, and the issuer shows it on its own line outside debt. Counting it lifts total debt to 9.19x last-twelve-month EBITDA, so the fixed ratios understate claims on the issuer's assets and the labelled alternative should be read beside them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No event after September 30, 2026 with a stated effect on net debt was found. In October 2026 American exercised purchase options for five Airbus A320 Family aircraft and committed to purchase two Boeing 777-200ER aircraft in the fourth quarter; no price or financing is stated for them individually, so they stay out of period figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is the size of liquidity against the principal due before the end of 2027: all of the issuer's debt principal is listed as secured, much of it amortises, maturities run out to 2039, and short-term investments have grown during 2026. That would win if fuel prices fall and quarterly EBITDA recovers toward the FY2025 level, so the observable tests are quarterly operating income, fuel cost, the customer-funded balances and the liquidity figure at the next filing. A downside sequence begins with another fuel price rise or a booking slowdown, first breaks operating cash conversion because customer-funded balances unwind, and then draws on short-term investments to service the 2027 and 2028 principal, which would show as lower liquidity before it shows as a covenant event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA is derived as operating income plus depreciation and amortization because the issuer states none, and it keeps special items inside operating income; the interim ratios use last-twelve-month figures built from reported full-year and nine-month amounts. Net debt deducts the cash line only, so the fixed net leverage is higher than readings that also deduct short-term investments, which are not shown to be unrestricted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, ownership, new debt and governance facts for AMERICAN AIRLINES, INC. (american-airlines-inc), as of 2026-11-05, under the credit_snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's own business and its relationship with its parent, using the annual report for 2025 and the third-quarter 2026 report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: American is wholly owned by its parent with no sponsor, and creditors' main governance risk is cash lent upstream to the parent rather than retained: the net receivable from the parent reached USD 12,512 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The parent otherwise looks supportive: it guarantees the issuer's credit facilities and the AAdvantage financing, the issuer's equity statement shows no dividend, and 2026 financing refinanced and extended debt rather than restructuring it. Governance detail for the issuer itself is omitted from the annual report, so board control and related-party terms are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer's cash is moving to its parent as loans, not dividends. The net receivable from the parent was USD 12,512 million at September 30, 2026 against USD 11,938 million at year-end, and the annual report says part of the earlier increase was American funding the parent's USD 1.0 billion cash settlement of its convertible notes in July 2025. Cash lent this way is no longer available to repay American's own debt until the parent repays it, so the parent's liquidity and refinancing ability matter to the issuer's creditors; repayment terms are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The parent supports the issuer's debt rather than extracting from it. It guarantees American's credit facilities as a senior unsecured obligation, guarantees the AAdvantage notes and term loans together with special-purpose guarantors, and has in certain cases guaranteed equipment notes, while the issuer's equity statement shows no dividend paid and the parent paid no cash dividend or share repurchase in 2025 or 2024. The guarantees are only as strong as the parent's own balance sheet, which carries separate debt outside the issuer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The loyalty program gives the business an unusually durable cash source. Loyalty revenue was 13.42% of operating revenues in the first nine months of 2026, and the group received USD 6.2 billion of cash from co-branded card and other partners in 2025, but the same program carries the largest customer-funded liability and also backs the AAdvantage secured financing, so a weaker partner relationship would hit liquidity and collateral together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost flexibility is limited and fuel is unhedged. Salaries, wages and benefits were 30.18% of operating expenses in the first nine months of 2026, about 86% of the group's employees are covered by labour contracts, and the group had no fuel hedges outstanding at the end of 2025 under a policy not to hedge. Margins therefore move with fuel prices and wage settlements and not with management cost actions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_aal-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_aal-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 110; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financing in 2026 was creditor-neutral to constructive, but it added secured debt. American extended its revolving facilities to 2031, refinanced and upsized its 2014 term loan to a 2033 maturity, repaid its short-term term loan, prepaid the 8.50% senior secured notes and issued three new aircraft and engine pass-through certificate series plus equipment loans. Cash-flow proceeds exceeded payments by USD 590 million for the nine months even after retirements of USD 1,939 million, so the effect is a longer, more secured maturity profile and not a smaller debt stock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance transparency for the issuer is thin. American omits the executive, director and ownership items of its annual report under the reduced-disclosure rules, the parent's proxy statement was not supplied, and the audit opinion and controls conclusions are clean, so the weakness is missing detail, not adverse findings. The parent's tax benefit preservation plan, which runs to October 2027, deters certain share acquisitions and so lowers the chance of a tax-driven ownership change during that period.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against concern is that lending to the parent is intragroup, the parent guarantees much of the issuer's debt, and the issuer reports USD 11,763 million of available liquidity with no dividend leakage. If the parent repays the receivable or discloses that it is repayable on demand, the governance risk would fall to low; if the receivable keeps growing while earnings weaken, or the parent funds distributions, buybacks or its own long-dated debt maturities from American's cash, the risk would rise to high.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The repayment terms and security of the receivable from the parent are not stated, so the finding that cash is trapped upstream may overstate the risk if the balance is repayable on demand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Board, control, fee and sponsor-style disclosure for the issuer is omitted, so the medium governance risk level rests on observed behaviour, not on control rights.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No executed agreements were supplied, so the finding that 2026 financing was creditor-neutral rests on the filings' descriptions of terms, and guarantee scope beyond those descriptions is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Nothing dated after October 22, 2026 was supplied, so later financing, distributions or litigation outcomes could change the behaviour findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No acquisition, sponsor transaction or change of control is stated for the issuer, so the summary is of its 2026 debt activity. In February 2026 the 2025 AAdvantage term loan was amended to lower its margin, and in March 2026 the three revolving facilities were re-established with commitments to March 2031. In May 2026 the 2014 term loan was refinanced and increased to a May 2033 maturity, and aircraft and engine financing continued through three pass-through certificate programs in May, June and August 2026 and USD 705 million of new equipment loans.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer also retired debt: the short-term term loan, which was due in January 2026, was repaid in full, the 8.50% senior secured notes were prepaid in full, and USD 310 million of equipment notes under earlier pass-through certificates was prepaid. Of the August 2026 certificates, about USD 633 million of proceeds was still held in escrow at September 30, 2026 and is not reported as debt until further equipment notes are issued, so reported debt excludes that amount for now.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by cash lent to the parent and by thin governance disclosure, because both reduce what creditors can see and recover from the issuer's own cash, which implies reliance on the parent's credit. Countervailing evidence is the parent's guarantees, the absence of dividends and a clean audit. Further analysis requires the terms of the receivable and the parent's proxy statement.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for AMERICAN AIRLINES, INC. (american-airlines-inc), as of 2026-11-05, under the credit_snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's business, financial profile, downside path and monitoring triggers, built from the supplied analyses and the issuer's filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: American's fundamental credit profile is adequate but strained: a large hub-and-loyalty business and USD 11,763 million of liquidity support creditors, while fuel-driven earnings pressure has lifted total debt to 8.87x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA and left interest cover at 2.06x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C03

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside path is another fuel spike or demand slowdown that cuts EBITDA while customer-funded cash unwinds, drawing on liquidity that covers principal due through 2028 only 0.98x. Refinancing capacity rests on aircraft collateral and loyalty assets, and the parent relationship adds support through guarantees and risk through USD 12,512 million of cash lent upstream.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C03; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is high because earnings fell, not because debt grew. Reported EBITDA fell from USD 4,573 million in FY2024 to USD 2,916 million over the last twelve months while debt stayed near USD 25,876 million, taking total debt to 8.87x; unhedged fuel and contract-bound labour costs pass price shocks straight into EBITDA, so creditors carry fuel risk without a cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest cover is thin. Interest paid took 48.56% of last-twelve-month EBITDA, so cover of 2.06x leaves little room before cash interest competes with maturities and aircraft deliveries for liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is the main protection but is finite. USD 11,763 million of available liquidity covers the USD 4,181 million of principal due before the end of 2027 by 2.81x, yet it only matches the USD 12,042 million due through 2028, so access to refinancing, not cash on hand, decides the 2028 outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Recent cash flow is flattered by customer-funded balances. Free cash flow of USD 1,780 million in the first nine months of 2026 came with a USD 3,206 million rise in air traffic and loyalty liabilities, which unwind if bookings slow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Support from the parent is real but runs both ways. The parent guarantees the issuer's credit facilities and the AAdvantage financing and no dividend is evidenced, yet the issuer has lent USD 12,512 million net to the parent, so the issuer's liquidity is partly a claim on the parent group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case that the view is too cautious is that last-twelve-month EBITDA is depressed by a fuel spike: fuel cost rose 55.22% in nine months while revenue grew 15.63%, the parent guides to continued growth in fourth-quarter revenue, and 2026 financing pushed the revolving facilities to 2031 and a term loan to 2033. A fall in fuel prices that restores EBITDA toward the FY2025 level would cut leverage from 8.87x toward 7.44x without any debt reduction. The view would turn more negative if liquidity fell below the principal due before the end of 2027, if the receivable from the parent grew while earnings weakened, or if refinancing of the 2028 maturities needed additional collateral beyond aircraft.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ranked weaknesses. First, high leverage driven by fuel: reported EBITDA of USD 2,916 million over the last twelve months against debt of USD 25,876 million gives 8.87x, and unhedged fuel passes price shocks directly to earnings, which leaves little capacity to absorb another shock. Second, thin cover of 2.06x with interest paid at 48.56% of EBITDA, which raises the cost of any shortfall. Third, a 2028 maturity of USD 7,861 million that exceeds what liquidity covers alone. Fourth, debt that is entirely secured, with 55.75% linked to aircraft and engines, so more borrowing adds claims on the same collateral. Fifth, a net receivable from the parent of USD 12,512 million, which makes the issuer's cash partly dependent on the parent's credit.

fields.value: Ranked strengths. First, liquidity of USD 11,763 million including USD 7,159 million of short-term investments, which covers principal due before the end of 2027 by 2.81x. Second, a network and loyalty business in which loyalty revenue was 13.42% of revenue and partners paid USD 6.2 billion of cash to the group in 2025, a recurring source that supports financing against loyalty assets. Third, demonstrated refinancing access in 2026, when revolvers were extended to 2031, a term loan to 2033 and three aircraft certificate programs were placed. Fourth, a parent that guarantees key debt and paid no dividend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: American is a network carrier that sells scheduled passenger and cargo service through nine hubs, with regional carriers flying under capacity purchase agreements, and it is wholly owned by its parent. Domestic routes were 70.89% of passenger revenue in the first nine months of 2026 and loyalty revenue 13.42% of operating revenues, so the business draws on passenger demand across its network and on a loyalty program whose partner cash and mileage balances act as recurring funding. No customer concentration is stated. The group structure matters for creditors: the parent guarantees American's credit facilities and the AAdvantage financing, but it carries its own debt and has received USD 12,512 million of net cash from the issuer, so the issuer is both supported by and a funder of the group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical and partly discretionary but backed by loyalty income: revenue grew 15.63% in the nine months to September 30, 2026, so demand has held, yet pricing power did not offset fuel, whose cost rose 55.22%. Costs are largely fixed in the short run because about 86% of the group's employees are covered by labour contracts and fuel is unhedged by policy, which means margins shrink first when fuel rises, and creditors rather than management cost actions carry the gap. Capital intensity is high, with USD 24,056 million of aircraft and engine commitments against nine-month capital expenditures of USD 2,660 million, and free cash flow of USD 1,780 million in the nine months was helped by a USD 3,206 million rise in customer-funded balances, so durable conversion of EBITDA to debt service cash is not yet shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competition is intense and the filings list competitive, regulatory, labour and fuel risks as the main pressures; the credit translation is that sector pricing and cost shocks reach earnings faster than debt can be reduced. Rivalry and fuel are the forces that move margins, while supplier concentration in aircraft and engines delays deliveries and raises financing needs. Regulatory and policy factors matter through antitrust litigation at the parent group and aviation regulation, and macroeconomic demand matters through leisure and corporate travel; none of these has a quantified effect in the sources. In credit terms the supportive items are network scale, loyalty cash and a parent that guarantees debt, and the constraining items are leverage, fuel exposure and secured-debt concentration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are adequate: the network is broad but no market share is stated. Competitive advantage rests on the loyalty program and hubs and is adequate. Business diversification is weak to adequate, with 70.89% of passenger revenue domestic and no customer data. Cost and capex flexibility are weak, because labour is contracted, fuel is unhedged and commitments are large. Margin stability is weak: the EBITDA margin on the nine months fell with fuel. Free cash flow stability is weak to adequate because recent strength depends on customer-funded balances. Ability to refinance is adequate, evidenced by 2026 transactions but limited by secured-only debt and the group's non-investment-grade corporate credit rating. Liquidity is adequate for the next five quarters and only matches principal through 2028. Financial policy and governance are adequate: no dividend and parent guarantees, offset by cash lent to the parent. The trend is down on leverage and cover and flat on liquidity, and the missing data are executed agreements, covenant headroom and the terms of the receivable from the parent.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over twelve to twenty-four months the parent guides to fourth-quarter revenue growth of 19.5% to 22.5% and a full-year 2026 adjusted loss per share of USD (1.60) to USD (1.00), on an assumed fuel price of about USD 4.70 per gallon, so earnings stay under pressure through year-end and leverage on trailing EBITDA is unlikely to improve before 2027. Tailwinds are revenue growth, loyalty cash, extended maturities and loyalty cash; headwinds are fuel, contract wage increases and the USD 7,861 million 2028 maturity. Over three to five years the question is whether fleet renewal funded by secured debt lifts margins enough to reduce leverage; the sources give no issuer-level forecast, so that is not established.

fields.value: Basis: EX-99.2_2026-10-22_earningspresentation.htm.jsonl, page 6; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C03; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The supported downside begins with fuel staying near the parent's assumed level or rising, or with a booking slowdown. Revenue growth then fails to cover fuel, and because labour is contracted and fuel is unhedged, EBITDA falls below the USD 2,916 million last-twelve-month level and cover below 2.06x. Free cash flow turns negative as customer-funded balances stop rising, drawing on the USD 7,159 million of short-term investments, while aircraft commitments continue. Liquidity of USD 11,763 million is enough to avoid distress through 2027, but it only equals the principal due through 2028, so the first financial break would be refinancing of the 2028 maturities on secured terms against aircraft and loyalty collateral. Possible management levers are drawing the undrawn facilities and slowing lending to the parent, while deferral of aircraft deliveries is not established by the sources; resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis in 2027 and uncertain for 2028. No numerical stress result is established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, American presents an adequate business profile supported by a broad network, loyalty cash and liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 8.87x reported EBITDA, thin cover of 2.06x and unhedged fuel exposure. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but flattered by customer-funded balances. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on aircraft and loyalty collateral, market access for secured debt and the parent's credit, since the parent guarantees key debt and holds USD 12,512 million of the issuer's cash. The primary downside path is fuel-driven earnings compression that consumes liquidity before the 2028 maturities. Further analysis would require executed agreements, covenant headroom, the terms of the parent receivable and an issuer-level outlook. Top risk: fuel-driven earnings compression.
